title: P1: JSONL reader rounds high-significance decimal cells through f64
description: Read-only audit finding (2026-11-26, no source edits): production cargo tree -e features,normal resolves serde_json 1.0.154 with default + preserve_order, but without float_roundtrip, arbitrary_precision, or raw_value. cmdrvl-tabular src/jsonl_reader.rs:116-120 parses each object line into Value; :143-153 converts non-integer Numbers via as_f64()+canon_f64 into Cell bytes. This is a shared upstream data conversion: a 16-19 significant-digit JSON decimal can become the adjacent f64 value, changing downstream comparison/verdict/output values in rvl and shape. XLSX/Parquet native numeric paths are separate. No released tabular binary was present locally, so this audit is code-read only. NOT VERIFIED: no build, test, release-binary reproduction, or fix was run.

comments.author: zac
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED: cmdrvl-tabular commit f189e2d pushed to main; CI run 46181763225 completed successfully (wasm and quality).

Change: JSONL object values are captured as original tokens with serde_json raw_value, parsed by cmdrvl-core ExactDecimal at b586ad3, and emitted as exact semantic canonical Cell bytes via to_key_string. No arbitrary_precision and no float_roundtrip. JSON strings still decode as strings; nested values remain E_UNSUPPORTED_VALUE. Every DecimalError variant is mapped to a typed E_UNSUPPORTED_VALUE with stable kind/ reason/ row/column context and no number text leak. The public Cell, Row, Table, open, open_bytes and RefusalCode APIs are unchanged; Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock now add the approved core dependency and raw_value feature only.

Failing-negative evidence: before the fix, jsonl_numbers_use_exact_semantic_values_from_original_tokens failed because 9007199254740992.1 and .2 both became 9007199254740992 through f64. After the fix it passes, with those values distinct; 1, 1.0, 1.00 and 1e0 all become 1; 100 and 1e2 both become 100; the JSON string "1.0" stays "1.0". The path/open_bytes parity test passes. 1e1025 is a value-free typed exponent_out_of_range refusal; 1e1024 and 1e-1024 are accepted exactly at the supported boundary.

Output/API delta against current tabular main: the 10-cell regression fixture covers 2 previously-colliding high-significance values, 6 equal-spelling numeric cases, signed zero, and a string; only the two colliding values change in that ordinary fixture. The boundary fixture adds two values that the old f64 path refused as non-finite; beyond-range integer/exponent spellings now remain exact rather than rounded. Existing ordinary JSONL canonical bytes (1.50 -> 1.5, 1e3 -> 1000, -0 -> 0) remain unchanged. Non-JSONL formats and all existing refusal/output contracts remain green. Consumer impact: rvl and shape need their cmdrvl-tabular pin and direct cmdrvl-core pin reviewed together at adoption; profile and benchmark need the tabular pin bump and JSONL fixture/output review; verify-duckdb uses tabular for XLSX only, so its pin is dependency-only for this change; fingerprint has no direct tabular consumer. rvl/shape exact non-key numeric comparison remains rollout step 3.

Checks:
- lockf -k /private/tmp/spine-cargo-2.lock env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=3 cargo test -- --test-threads=1: 98 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored, 0 doctests.
- lockf -k /private/tmp/spine-cargo-2.lock env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=3 cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings: passed.
- lockf -k /private/tmp/spine-cargo-2.lock env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=3 cargo fmt --check: passed.
- lockf -k /private/tmp/spine-cargo-2.lock env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=3 cargo tree -e features -p cmdrvl-tabular: only cmdrvl-core b586ad3 and serde_json raw_value matched; no arbitrary_precision or float_roundtrip.
- UBS_SKIP_RUST_BUILD=1 ubs Cargo.toml Cargo.lock README.md src/lib.rs src/jsonl_reader.rs tests/open_bytes.rs tests/refusals.rs: critical=0.
- Core oracle generator commit 58b0de3 reproduces tests/fixtures/exact_decimal_oracle.json byte-for-byte (cmp exit 0).

NOT VERIFIED: downstream consumer pin commits, released rvl/shape/profile/benchmark binaries, Linux/Windows execution, full consumer output/capsule/witness compatibility, and any rollout after tabular. No releases or consumer pushes were made.

title: open and open_bytes panic on some corrupted Parquet files instead of returning a typed refusal
description:
Found by the orchestrator while verifying spine-rules bd-nh4. Three corrupted Parquet files (fixture bytes with random flips or truncation) panic in open()/open_bytes() or while reading rows, at 57c3085 (before open_bytes) and at e83afb0 alike, so it predates that change: 24 panicking file/option cases of 25402. Expected: a typed refusal, never a panic. NOT CHECKED: the panic message and location, and whether released shape or rvl binaries are affected. Smallest reproducer, 753 bytes, base64 (decode to a .parquet file, open with default options):

close_reason: Verified by orchestrator at 4ccf1d3 (evidence a97ed9c), CI green. Returned once (a second corrupted file still panicked and one refusal had changed). Exact export, touched and built: refusals 37 and open_bytes 8 passed; no removed asserts or tests, no suppressions, no catch_unwind. Own differential over 25402 file and option cases vs e83afb0: 24 panics before, 0 now, all 24 now EParquetParse; every other outcome identical; open_bytes equals open. NOT verified: panic paths inside the parquet dependency (that inspection was blocked and stayed undone), fuzzing beyond this corpus and the repo test, full suite locally (CI), wasm runtime, whether released shape or rvl crash on these files, consumers (they pin e83afb0 or older and need a pin bump to get the fix). NOT RELEASED.

comments.text:
Implemented and pushed as 4ccf1d3.

Failing-first: before the fix, the second 3038-byte corrupt-Parquet regression
test failed for the bytes path after the parquet dependency panicked with
"Decoder for dict should have been set" (the path result also did not produce
the required typed refusal). I did not inspect parquet dependency source or
dependency panic paths, because the earlier dcg inspection timed out and the
instruction was not to repeat or obtain that information another way.

Fix: validate impossible Parquet dictionary metadata before lazy row decoding:
negative/invalid page ranges, dictionary offsets at or after data offsets, and
dictionary encodings without a dictionary page now return the existing
E_PARQUET_PARSE refusal. The existing footer max_rows check remains first, so
the prior max_rows=1 case continues to return E_TOO_LARGE rather than changing
refusal precedence. No catch_unwind is used in product code and no dependency
or manifest change was made.
